message.content: {"summary":"Excellent work on the ZYZZsat mission design report. All required elements are addressed with verified hand calculations, STK evidence and clear referencing. To reach the very top of the rubric, add the X-band link budget, tighten loosely specified references, and make the conclusion more quantitative.","next_steps":["Complete the X-band link budget for Section 2.4 to substantiate the assumed 50 Mbit/s downlink, showing margin for the six daily passes.","Quantify the four limitations listed in your conclusion (e.g. decay uncertainty range, link margin) so conclusions are directly traceable to evidence.","Replace loosely specified references such as [4] and [15] with fully cited sources, and consider a brief user-needs analysis for AIMS/GBRMPA in Section 1."],"criteria":{"C1":"Accomplished (9/10). Your introduction thoroughly covers the primary mission (5 m GBR imaging), rationale with literature, single-spacecraft justification, and operator/customers. Next level: add a short user-needs analysis showing how AIMS and GBRMPA requirements drive the 5 m resolution and revisit choices.","C2":"Accomplished (9/10). Comprehensive design: justified Vega C/Kourou trade, verified J2 sun-sync inclination (97.79°), STK access tables, data budget and EOL plan. Next level: perform the X-band link budget you flagged as missing, and discuss quantitatively how the Vega C unflown-status risk affects your fallback choice.","C3":"Accomplished (8/10). Conclusions follow from your evidence and honestly state limitations and next-phase actions. Next level: summarise key quantitative results (orbit elements, pass statistics, decay time, data volumes) in the conclusion so it stands alone as a design summary.","C4":"Accomplished (9/10). Clear structure, concise executive summary, well-labelled figures/tables, and in-text citations [1]–[15] matching the bibliography. Next level: ensure every reference is fully specified (e.g. [4], [15]) so all sources are independently traceable."}}
